articles.title: An Oklahoma man bought a house in 2015 and later began renting it out for short stays, prompting complaints about late-night parties and noise; now, the state Supreme Court has upheld $8,528 in HOA assessments and penalties, along with an injunction barring his short-term rental business
articles.summary: The Oklahoma Supreme Court has upheld a lower court ruling against an Edmond homeowner who used his property for short-term rentals, finding that the
articles.body: The Oklahoma Supreme Court has upheld a lower court ruling against an Edmond homeowner who used his property for short-term rentals, finding that the practice violated the Silverhawk community’s restrictive covenants. The decision closes a dispute that began in 2019, when the man started renting out his home to guests, contrary to the homeowners’ association (HOA) rules. In a decision on 11 November, the court upheld the injunction barring short-term rentals and the $8,528 in fines imposed by the association.Turning his home into short-term rentalsThe man bought the house in the Silverhawk neighbourhood of Edmond, Oklahoma, in 2015. A few years later, he began renting it to short-term guests through platforms such as Airbnb. The man claims he consulted the board before renting out the property. In October 2019, he contacted the neighbourhood association about renting out the house. ‘I don't see anything that stops you from doing that,’ one board member reportedly told him. That, however, was not an approval. The man argues that he did not interpret the response as a refusal. ‘But I didn't feel her response was explicit enough to tell me that, so that's why I took my next step.’ He emailed the group's secretary, who replied that the association did not restrict rentals. The man therefore took that as the answer he needed.The neighbourhood rule said ‘business’The HOA's rules were clear in some respects. They stated that the lots ‘shall be used for private residence purposes only’. They also specified that ‘no store or business’ could be built or maintained on any lot. However, nothing in the wording specifically mentioned renting to visitors for a few nights. The association argued that renting a property for money to a rotating group of guests constituted a business. The man argued that the term was too vague to be enforced against him.Noise complaints and moreWhen the dispute went to trial, a neighbour who lives directly behind the house described weekend groups using the backyard grill, some as large as fourteen people. She said the noise could reach her bedrooms as late as two or three in the morning. Another neighbour described large parties and more cars than a typical family would own. The man questioned both witnesses and pointed out that neither had complained to him directly or contacted the police. The trial court weighed their testimony, and the Supreme Court later said it would not second-guess that judgement.The Oklahoma County District Court heard the case in a five-day bench trial. The judge ruled that the rentals breached the covenant. The court issued an injunction against the business, awarded the association fines and assessments, and rejected the man's claim that the association had breached its contract with him. He represented himself.Unhappy with the decision, the man appealed. The Court of Civil Appeals, in a divided ruling, reversed much of that decision. The HOA took the matter to the Oklahoma Supreme Court. Five justices joined the majority opinion by Justice Edmondson, which vacated the appeals court's decision and affirmed the trial court's judgement. The majority said the covenant's language was clear and that the ordinary meaning of ‘business’ applied to property rules just as it did to contracts and tax law.Four justices dissented. They argued that the word ‘business’ describes what a building is used for, not how people occupy it. The dissent said guests who sleep, cook and grill at a house are living there as a home, even for a short time, and that the court should not add a rule that the covenant never states.The court also declined to review the attorney's fee award because the man had not raised the issue in the proper manner. This means the trial court's decision on fees remains in place.However, the homeowner's frustration has not faded following the ruling. ‘Over five exhausting years, the very institutions meant to protect homeowners betrayed me,’ he told NonDoc, a local news outlet that covered the case. He said he had to file for bankruptcy to protect his home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Daily Astrology News Alert, 12 November 2026: Mars Leaves Weak Cancer as Moon Shifts to Sagittarius, Lost Energy and Courage Start Returning
articles.summary: Thursday feels like waking up after a long, heavy nap. Mars ends its debilitated stay in Cancer tonight and moves into Leo.
articles.body: Thursday feels like waking up after a long, heavy nap. Mars ends its debilitated stay in Cancer tonight and moves into Leo. The Moon has already left Scorpio for Sagittarius. Both changes lift the mood. Tasks that felt like climbing uphill begin to move with less effort.Mars Moves from Cancer to LeoMars spent weeks in Cancer struggling to act with confidence. Anger stayed bottled up, and effort often went in circles. Leo is a fire sign ruled by the Sun, a friend of Mars. Here the planet regains its drive and directness.Courage returns first. People may finally make the phone call they kept postponing or speak up in a meeting after weeks of silence. But tonight’s shift takes a day or two to show its full effect, so begin slowly.Mars Joins Jupiter and Ketu in LeoOnce Mars enters Leo, it shares the sign with Jupiter and Ketu. Mars with Jupiter forms Guru-Mangal Yoga, often linked with righteous action and leadership. Mars with Ketu, though, can make people hasty and prone to minor injuries.Use the new energy for planned work. Avoid rash driving, sudden quarrels or lifting heavy weights without help. From Leo, Mars also aspects Saturn in Pisces, so frustration may come from slow-moving systems like government offices or bank processes.Sagittarius Moon in Mula NakshatraThe Moon travels through Mula, a Ketu-ruled nakshatra whose name means “root.” Mula pulls things out by the roots to start afresh. People may want to clear clutter, end an old habit or rethink a belief that no longer helps.Thursday is ruled by Jupiter, the lord of Sagittarius. Jupiter also aspects the Moon from Leo. Hope and faith feel stronger. Saturn’s tenth aspect on Sagittarius, though, keeps that hope grounded in practical action.Recovery After the Festive WeekAfter Diwali and Bhai Dooj, many people feel drained. This combination supports gentle recovery. A morning walk, a proper breakfast and a full night’s sleep will help Mars’s returning energy settle in without strain.Signs to WatchLeo prepares to host Mars along with Jupiter and Ketu. Confidence rises sharply, but so does impatience. Count to ten before replying to criticism.Cancer feels relief as Mars leaves its sign. Tension at home starts easing, and sleep may improve.Sagittarius carries the Moon with Jupiter’s support. Optimism returns, and a delayed personal plan may get a green signal.Aries, ruled by Mars, gains energy for children’s matters and creative work. Scorpio, the other Mars sign, may feel more confident at work soon.Aquarius will soon receive Mars’s direct gaze across the zodiac. Partners may seem demanding. Stay calm and clear.Pisces faces Mars’s aspect on Saturn in its sign. Delays in health or paperwork may test patience.Gemini finds the Sagittarius Moon in its partnership area. A spouse may suggest a short trip.Taurus should handle joint finances carefully. Virgo may focus on home comfort and mother’s needs.Libra could hear from siblings or plan a short visit. Capricorn may want to rest and reduce expenses.Love, Career & MoneyLove: Couples who have been feeling distant can begin reconnecting through doing things together. Plan a short trip or watch a movie together. Single people may feel bolder in expressing interest.Career: Lost motivation is found again. Follow up on stalled projects and deadlines for next week. Avoid challenging authority too strongly once Mars enters Leo.Money: Your earning energy will improve, but don’t get swept up by a sudden burst of confidence and make risky trades. articles.title: Yella Beezy found guilty of hiring gunman to kill rapper MO3
articles.summary: Dallas rapper Yella Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, was convicted of capital murder by a Dallas County jury on Wednesday.
articles.body: Dallas rapper Yella Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, was convicted of capital murder by a Dallas County jury on Wednesday. He allegedly hired the gunman who killed fellow rapper MO3, born Melvin Noble.Beezy was sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, the Associated Press reported.“We don’t know what turned it for the jurors. We appreciate the verdict,” lead prosecutor Tommy Adams said. “We think they got it right today. It’s been one of the most challenging cases over the last six years.”According to the BBC, Beezy associate Kewon white was also convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Prosecutors identified White as the shooter who killed MO3 on a Dallas highway in November 2020.According to the prosecution, white pulled up alongside MO3’s vehicle on Interstate 35 in South Dallas, near the Dallas Zoo.
